awd_titl_txt: Conference: 2025 FASEB Science Research Conference on Septin GTPases
awd_abstract_narration:
Septins are a large family of proteins with essential functions for the organization and processes in cells. The conference will gather septin researchers from a breadth of disciplines, who do not regularly have the opportunity to interact in other scientific forums, to discuss recent findings and to forge new collaborations for tackling key unknowns and challenges. The conference will foster cohesiveness and long-term continuity by inviting speakers, who are new in this field of research, trainees and early career investigators. Sessions on real-life links and applications of septin research, along with emerging topics, will inspire and motivate attendees to pursue research having Broader Impacts on society that include animal and plant diseases. 

The program of the FASEB conference entitled "Septins – spatial regulators of cell biology" will feature sessions on problems of septin assembly and function in the morphogenesis of various cell types, and in cellular processes including cell division, cell migration, and intracellular force transduction. Researchers will present and discuss findings from studies that utilize structural, biophysical, genetic, biochemical and pharmacological methods. In addition to daily poster sessions, roundtable panels will facilitate direct interactions with speakers and mentoring discussions on career development. The schedule will also provide opportunities for group activities that will enable networking in a casual and informal setting.

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.

por.por_cntn:
Project Nature

The central goal of this conference was to bring together septin researchers from across the world, spanning academic, clinical, and biotechnology sectors and all career stages, for an interdisciplinary exchange of new scientific findings, community building, career development, and the forging of future research directions. The conference was the first such gathering in the United States in nearly 15 years, and the first anywhere in four years, making it a uniquely timely and important event for the field. The scientific program was designed to examine septins as regulators of diverse molecular mechanisms and cellular processes, and to explore their roles in disease pathogenesis and their potential applications for health and society. 

 

Project Outcomes

The conference attracted approximately 90 participants, with over half attending for the first time, reflecting the meeting's success in expanding and diversifying the septin research community. Participants included 40% trainees and 15% early-career investigators, underscoring the conference's strong investment in the next generation of researchers. The scientific program comprised eight sessions featuring 50 talks from invited speakers and submitted abstracts, three poster sessions, and three career development sessions tailored to trainees and early-career researchers. Structured networking opportunities, including daily meet-the-speaker sessions and evening socials, complemented the formal program and fostered new collaborative relationships across career stages and sectors. A particularly significant outcome is the publication of a special issue in Molecular Biology of the Cell journal, featuring a proceedings report alongside invited reviews and research articles from work presented at the conference. Additional peer-reviewed articles have already appeared from research presented and discussed during the meeting, demonstrating the conference's direct contribution to scientific dissemination and the advancement of the field. Attendee assessments were highly favorable, with an overall rating of 4.8 out of 5.0. Participants specifically rated the quality of the scientific program highly, and reported meaningful impacts on their research programs, career development, and professional networks, affirming that the conference achieved its broader scientific and educational goals. 

 

Broader Impacts

Beyond the exchange of unpublished scientific findings, the conference generated broad impacts across education, career development, and community building. Career development sessions provided trainees, graduate students, postdoctoral fellows, and junior investigators from both academia and biotechnology, with practical insights into diverse career pathways, including tenure-track and non-tenure-track academic positions, careers in biotechnology, and scientific publishing. These sessions fostered direct mentorship interactions between early-career scientists and established leaders across sectors. The deliberate inclusion of scientists from biotechnology companies and clinical research centers, together with dedicated sessions on real-world applications of septin biology to human health and disease, created an integrated forum bridging basic, applied, and translational research. Engagement of editors from leading scientific journals further strengthened the long-term dissemination of knowledge from this field to the broader scientific community and the public. Collectively, the conference served not only as a venue for scientific exchange but as an investment in the sustained growth of an internationally connected, career-diverse scientific community centered on septin biology.
